MAHINAY-SERO City Director DILG-Office of the City Director General Santos City Dear City Director Sero: DILGLe IO inion No. 24 s. 2012 08 2012 This refers to your 07 February 2012 letter on the LGU of General Santos' request for clarification regarding MC No. 2011-68, particularly the exception to the prohibition on the operation of tricycles and pedicabs along the National Highway in view of the following factual considerations: I. There are barangays in the city who cannot reach the city proper without travelling the national highways; 2. There is no alternative road available to reach the city proper however there are other available modes of transportation other than tricycles such as PUJs and franchised multicabs; 3. Article IV, Section I LGU's ordinance, denominated as #05, series of 1993, provides that: "I. For safety reasons, no tricycle should operate on national highways, utilized by four-wheel vehicles greater than four tons and where normal speed exceeds fifty kph However, the Sanggunian Pan/ungsod may provide exceptions if there are no other alternative route. " However, no legislation providing exception to the prohibition has been enacted by the SP of General Santos City. Below is a discussion on the issue, viz. : DILG MC No. 2011-68, which is a reiteration of DILG MC No. 2007-01 was issued by the Department to regulate the operations of tricycles and pedicabs rendering transport services to the general public pursuant to the DOTC's "Guidelines to Implement the Devolution of L TFRB's Franchising Authority Over Tricycles-For-Hire to Local Government Units Pursuant to the Local Government Code (RA No. 7160). " Under the Guidelines issued by the DOTC, as reiterated under DILG MC Nos. 2011-68 and 2007-01, 'For safety reasons, no tricycles should operate on national highways utilized by 4 wheel vehicles greater than 4 tons and where normal speed exceed 40 kph. However, the SB/SP may provide exceptions if there is no alternative route. " Municipalities and cities, through their respective sangguniangs, are granted the power to regulate the operation of tricycles and grant franchises within their respective territorial jurisdictions subject to the guidelines prescribed by the DOTC pursuant to Sections 447 (3) (vi) and 458 (3) (vi) of the Local Government. In the case "LTO vs. City of Butuan," G.R. 131512, January 20, 2000, the Supreme Court had the occasion to discuss the DOTC's (through the Land Transportation Franchising Regulatory Board) devolved power to grant franchises to tricycles-for-hire to the LGUs pursuant to the above-cited provisions of the Local Government Code, viz. : 'The Department of Transportation and Communicationsg ("DOT'), through the LTO and the LTFRB. has since been tasked with implementing laws pertaining to land transportation. x x x The L TFRB, upon the other hand, is the governing body tasked by E.O. No. 202, dated 19 June 1987, to regulate the operation of public utility or 'for hire* vehicles and to grant franchises or certificates of public convenience x x x

under the Local Government Code, certain functions of the DOTC were transferred to the LGUs, thusly: Sec. 458. Powers, Duties, Functions and Compensation. — xxx xxx xxx (3) Subject to the provisions of Book II of this Code, enact ordinances granting franchises and authorizing the issuance of permits or licenses, upon such conditions and for such purposes intended to promote the general welfare of the inhabitants of the city and pursuant to this legislative authority shall: xxx xxx xxx (VI) Subject to the guidelines prescribed by the Department of Transportation and Communications, regulate åe operation of tricycles and grant franchises for the operation thereof within fie territorial Jurisdiction of the city. (Emphasis supplied). LGUs indubitably now have the power to regulate the operation of tricycles-for-hire and to grant franchises for the operation thereof. 'To regulate' means to fix, establish, or control; to adjust by rufe, method, or established rnode; to direct by rule or restriction; or to subject to governing principles or Iqws. A franchise is defined to be a special privilege to do certain things conferred by government on an individual or corporation, and which does not belong to citizens generally Of common right.g x x x The devolution of the functions of the DOTC, performed by the LTFRB, to the LGUs, as so apt& observed by the Solicitor Genera', is aimed at curbing the alarming increase of accidents in national highways involving tricycles. It has been the perception that local governments are in good position to achieve the end desired by the law-making body because of their proximity to tfle situation that can enable them to address that serious concern better than the national govemment. It may not be amiss to state. nevertheless. that under Micle 458 of LQGQ!' Gpvqrnment Code. the power of LGUs to requJate the operation of tricvcles @ granf franchises for the operation thereof is still subject tQ the quidelines prescribed bv the DOTC. In compliance therewith, the Department of Transportation and Communication} ('DOTC') issued 'Guidelines to Implement the Devolution of L TFRBs Franchisinq Authority over to Local Government units pursuant to the Local Government Code. " Pertinent provisions of the guidelines state: In lieu of the Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) in the DOTC, the Sangguniang Bayan/Sangguniang Pang/ungsod (SB/SP) shall perform the following: (a) Issue, amend, revise, renew, suspend, or cancel MTOP and prescribe the appropriate terms and conditions therefor; xxx Operating Conditions: xxx xxx 1. For safety no tricycles should operate on national highways utilized bv 4 wheel vehicles greater than 4 tons and where normal speed exceed 40 KPH However, the SB/SP may provide exæptions if there is no altemative route. 2. Zones must be within the boundaries of the municipafdy/city. However, existing zones within more than one municipality/cäy shall be maintained, provided that operators serving said zone shall secure MTORs from each of the municipalities/cities having jurisdiction over the areas covered by the zone. 3. A common color for tricycles-for-hire operating in the same zone may be imposed Each unit shan be assigned and bear an identification number. aside from its L TO license plate number. 4. An operator wishing to stop service completely, or to suspend service for more than one month, should report in writing such termination or suspension to the SB/SP which originally granted the MTOP prior thereto, Transfer to another zone may be permitted upon application. 5, The WOP shall be valid for three (3) years, renewable for the same period. Transfer fo another zone, change of ownership of unit or transfer of MTOP Sha/l be construed as an amendment to an MTOP and shall require appropriate approval of the SB/SP. 6 Operators shall employ only drivers duly licensed by ITO for tricycles-for-hire. 7. NO tricycle-for-hire shall be allowed to carry more passengers and/or goods than it is designed for. 8. A tricycle-for-hire shall be allowed to operate like a taxi service, i.e., service is rendered upon demand and without a fixed route within a zone.ff'

It is therefore clear that under the GENERAL rule, tricycles and pedicabs are prohibited to operate along the national highway; the EXCEPTION to the prohibition is if there is NO ALTERNATIVE ROAD, as categorically provided for in an ordinance duly enacted by the Sanggunian. In this case, there is no ordinance categorically providing permission for tricycles and pedicabs along the national highway of General Santos City. SP Ordinance No. 05, s. 1993 is a mere restatement of paragraph no. I, Operating Conditions, of the DOTC's 1992 "Guidelines to Implement the Devolution of L TFRB's Franchising Authority Over Tricycles-For-Hire to Local Government Units Pursuant to the Local Government Code (RA No. 7160). " Notably, the power to allow tricyles-for-hire's operation along the national highway, as provided under the DOTC's Guidelines, rests with the LGUs' Sanggunian since it has a bird's eye view of the traffic situation within its territorial jurisdiction enabling it to come up with ordinances responsive to the general welfare of its inhabitants. Applying the foregoing premises, it is clear that the Sanggunian may, through an ordinance, allow the operation of tricyles-for-hire along the national highway under conditions set forth in the DOTC's Guidelines, as reiterated in DILG MC Nos. 2007-01 and 2011-68, provided that there is no alternative route. In the absence of an ordinance providing authority for their operation, tricycles and pedicabs are therefore prohibited from operating along the national highway. We hope to have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, ESUS Di recto LS08•xb cc DO 1 RD BUAGAS B. SULAIK, CESO Ill Sumpay Bk&., Block IV Mararm Vinage Bararvy Zone Ill, Koronadal City
